<thought>To achieve a one‑step synthesis of 4,4'-dimethoxystilbene (SMILES C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2) we can use a Wittig reaction. The reaction couples 4‑methoxybenzaldehyde with the commercially available phosphonium ylide precursor 4‑methoxybenzyltriphenylphosphonium bromide (or its pre‑formed ylide). This single transformation converts the aldehyde C=O into the C=C bond of the stilbene. Both reagents are inexpensive and readily purchasable, keeping the total cost well below $150. The retrosynthetic tree therefore has the target molecule as the root, a single reaction node (Wittig), and two leaf molecules that are commercially available.</thought>
